title: Breach of a non-disclosure agreement by an employee - employer remedies
p1:
An employee leaves the company… and suddenly your confidential information appears with a competitor. What can an employer actually do?

Many businesses assume signing an NDA means the problem is automatically solved. But an NDA is not just a document — it is a tool that can help protect valuable business information when used correctly.
p2: A surprising fact: not every piece of workplace information is automatically protected. Employers usually need to show that the information was genuinely confidential, that reasonable steps were taken to protect it, and that the employee misused or shared it without permission.
p3:
If a breach happens, employers may seek remedies such as stopping further disclosure through court orders, claiming compensation for losses, or taking action based on employment agreements. The strongest cases often come from businesses that clearly define confidential information before any dispute arises.

The practical takeaway? An NDA works best when combined with proper data controls, employee awareness, and clear policies — not when it is treated as a one-time signature exercise.
conclusion: Have you seen situations where an employee shared confidential company information after leaving a job? What measures do you think employers should take to prevent it?
